description: Every night the person reviews the day and writes a few sentences capturing the single most 'storyworthy' moment in a running spreadsheet/journal, building a searchable archive of personal story seeds over time.

A timed, nonjudgmental free-writing session where you write continuously and bounce between unrelated ideas/memories to surface forgotten stories and unexpected connections ('dreaming with the tip of your pen').
Take a mundane prompt word (e.g. car, meal, love, job) and write the story of your first, last, best, and worst experience of it; each cell becomes a potential story.
Identify the single instant in a story where something fundamentally changes forever, then build the whole telling around revealing that moment of transformation.
Open the story by stating the clear need/problem/mystery everyone can 'see' so the audience knows a story (not chitchat) has begun and what to anticipate.
Just before a pivotal moment, load the audience with the character's hopes, fears, and plans to raise stakes, so the payoff (especially when plans fail) lands harder.
At the point of peak audience anticipation, deliberately slow the narrative down to stretch tension and maximize the impact of the coming revelation.
Make a reasonable-but-false prediction to the audience to set up suspense over whether it will come true, creating a misdirect.
Rewrite story beats so they connect with 'but' or 'therefore' (cause/conflict) rather than 'and' (mere sequence), forcing each beat to show change.
Seed a key piece of information early, far from its payoff and camouflaged (often with humor), so the later reveal detonates with surprise.
Begin the story as the emotional/situational opposite of how it ends so the arc visibly shows a transformation of the self.
In small Zoom workshops participants craft and tell true 5-minute first-person stories, get coached on structure/stakes, and revise; Moth/StorySLAM-style live practice with feedback.

Solo rehearsal drill: deliver your conversational lines to a blank wall to practice with zero feedback/pressure. Level 1 basic conversation, Level 2 establishing the premise, Level 3 delivering a high-value frame.

Practice starting conversations using a chosen opener type (direct, direct-friendly/push-pull, situational/tease, opinion, impersonal); beginners drilled on the direct opener to get the interaction going.
Drill the 'man assessing woman' frame: communicate intent and position yourself as the one evaluating her for a role in your life rather than seeking approval.
Practice asking questions and prompts that get her to 'work' or convince you, screening her while raising your perceived value.
Construct and deliver the shared story of the two of you meeting, weaving a connecting narrative thread through the interaction.
Practice the four close moves: seed the idea before asking, frame the next step as a win for her, qualify, and lead by assuming the close with confidence.
Watch 8+ hours of real recorded approaches/dates by Todd and instructor JP with line-by-line commentary, then model the analyzed techniques in your own attempts.
Go out and approach women applying the system, then report results (field reports/assignments) for coaching, especially in bootcamp and mentorship tiers.

exercise_name: Verbal Game Academy Isolation Drills (openers, push-pull, emotional spikes)
description: In the 8-week Verbal Game Academy, drills isolate one skill at a time (openers, push-pulls, emotional spikes, shit-test deflection, sexual-premise injection) for focused reps, plus twice-weekly live webinars and mission Q&A.

Five-step setup-generation drill: (1) list topics you think are wrong, (2) make an association list of specific details, (3) form negative 'punch-premises', (4) flip them into positive 'setup-premises', (5) write short misdirecting setups.

Punchline-writing drill applying the joke mechanisms — find the Target Assumption the setup creates, choose a Connector (one thing with two meanings), and write a Reinterpretation that surprises the audience.
Deconstruct existing jokes into Setup -> Assumptions -> Connector -> Reinterpretation -> Punchline, training you to see and build the hidden second meaning ('1 thing with 2 meanings').
Record an unedited stream-of-consciousness rant about something that bothers you, then transcribe and mine the specifics ('the jokes are in the details') into setups and a routine script.

Stage your story by switching among Narrator POV (talking to the audience), Self POV (acting as yourself in the scene), and Character POV (playing other characters), physically acting out the funny moments.
Engage audience members with questions, repeat and extract details from their answers, and riff playfully to generate spontaneous jokes.
In a collaborative group, pitch jokes, take feedback, and add 'tags' (extra punchlines off the same setup) to extend a joke; build on others' ideas.
A rehearsal method to mentally separate and silence the inner critic so you stop 'practicing self-doubt' and rehearse with confidence; assemble and warm up before performing.
Practice handling the mic, stand, and cord until 'the mic becomes invisible' so equipment never distracts from the performance.

Structured exercise sets across five workbooks: Workbook 1 How to Write Jokes, plus improving jokes/routines, How to Remember Jokes Naturally, funny performing, and How to Get the Experience to Be Funny.

exercise_name: 48 Exercises to Turn Problems into Punchlines
description: A sequential workbook of 48 exercises that walk the comic from personal problems/anger to finished punchlines; includes finding authentic topics, mind-mapping your best 3 topics, ranting to laughs, and structuring jokes.
Thirty daily writing prompts to generate raw comedy material and build a writing habit, captured in the workbook.

exercise_name: Find Your Authentic Topics / Mind-Map Top 3
description: Identify what genuinely angers or excites you, then mind-map your three strongest topics as the source of personal material.
Rewrite jokes to replace narration with physically/vocally acting out the moment (a term Carter coined), making bits show rather than tell.

exercise_name: List of Three / Rule of Three
description: Build a list where the unexpected third item creates the laugh; drill the comedic-triple structure.
Craft a strong opening bit and add callbacks (re-using an earlier punchline near the end) to close the set strong.
Define your stage persona and point of view (attitude toward the topic) so material is consistent and authentic.
Practice engaging the audience and using prepared responses/comebacks to handle hecklers and stay in control.
1-on-1/workshop process to add jokes and tighten the comedic angle of a speech, message, or even emails for professionals and speakers.
Day-by-day bootcamp-style workshop where comics develop, perform, and sharpen a set with hands-on feedback; set-list building from polished jokes by topic.
Voice exercises to control pitch, cadence, and tone and to eliminate filler words and vocal tics — e.g. practicing downward inflection and slowing speech.
A primer and practice routine for opening conversations with anyone, anywhere — initiating cold approaches and starting interactions on demand.

exercise_name: Five Fundamentals of a Solid Approach (Toolbox Ep. 664)
description: Practice making and breaking eye contact at the right times, showing enthusiasm, holding neutral body language, and demonstrating commitment to the approach.
Apply the three levels of rapport, learning to use each and to gauge whether you are actually building rapport with the right people.
Structured exercises for building and telling compelling personal narratives/stories in conversation.
In the 5-day residential bootcamp, participants do conversation/approach role-plays in morning group workshops (9-11am) and get live feedback plus 1-on-1 coaching (11am-1pm).
Assigned missions throughout the bootcamp week to go out and apply skills (approach strangers, hold conversations, network) in real venues, then debrief.
Workshops to identify unhelpful mindsets and limiting beliefs and do reflective work to build a growth mindset and overcome insecurities.

Online program practicing 8 named frameworks (Intrigue, Elicitation Protocol, High-Value OS, Identity Markers, Value Flywheel, Social Capital Networking, Aura, Social Sales Funnel) with weekly Language Labs, an AI coach for rehearsing high-stakes conversations, and a peer cohort.
Drills for converting acquaintances into advocates and building social capital — practical networking reps and follow-up techniques.
